newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU studies beef crisis budget balancing act.
newsitem.headline: EU studies beef crisis budget balancing act.

text.p: The European Commission will study ways of advancing up to 1.2 billion Ecus of 1997 farm spending so that it is paid before the current financial year ends on October 15, Irish Farm Minister Ivan Yates said.
The funds would help compensate beef producers hit by an 11 percent slump in EU beef demand due to a public health scare over mad cow disease.
The Commission will also present complementary financing proposals by the next EU farm ministers' meeting.
"We'll press ahead for an agreement at the end of October," Yates told a news conference after a two-day EU farm council.
But he said there was still wide discord over the Commission's proposals to reduce beef and veal production and curb growing surpluses.
The main disagreements were between supporters of grass-fed and intensive production methods and over plans to cut aid to cereals farmers by seven percent so as to fund the beef aid.
But the European Parliament had now agreed to give an opinion by September 20, clearing the way for a formal decision, Yates said.

He added that EU farm ministers, meeting informally in Killarney, Ireland, next week will discuss how to continue buying surplus beef into intervention stores after the 1996 ceiling of 400,000 tonnes is reached in early October.

The Commission, warning that the beef market would otherwise collapse, has proposed increasing the ceiling to 720,000 tonnes but this was part of a package of measures on which no agreement was possible this week. --Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
